Constitutive model audit¶

The active registry now includes bingham, dp, dp_rate, and linear_mu, as well as the five previously converted laws. These four kernels are array based and checked against analytical responses and physical invariants. The old scalar code is historical evidence, not the numerical reference for these models.

All tensors are 3 by 3, including the out-of-plane normal stress in plane strain. Cauchy stress is tension positive. Below, p = -tr(stress)/3 is compression positive, s = stress + p I, q = sqrt(3/2 s:s), and the engineering equivalent shear rate is gamma = sqrt(2 D':D'), with D' = dev(dstrain)/dt. Particles.p and .q compute these invariants from current stress. The existing .pressure diagnostic remains tension positive; for Bingham it stores the elastic mean part, excluding instantaneous bulk-viscous stress.

Restored laws¶

Law

Parameters (SI units)

Behaviour and corrections

bingham

K >= 0 (Pa), mu_s >= 0, mu_0 > mu_s, optional mu_v >= 0 (Pa s), tau_0 >= 0 (Pa)

Continuous bi-viscosity regularisation, correct stress-increment interface, engineering shear invariant, dissipative bulk viscosity.

dp

K, G > 0 (Pa), mu > 0, 0 <= beta <= mu

Cohesionless, perfectly plastic Drucker–Prager solid with nonassociated dilation and a zero mean-tensile-strength cutoff. Replaces the singular legacy H²/loading-direction formula with a return map.

dp_rate

Same as dp, plus t_star >= 0 (s)

Linear Perzyna overstress regularisation, integrated by backward Euler. Replaces a rate update missing its timestep factor.

linear_mu

K >= 0 (Pa), mu_0, b >= 0, rho_s > 0 (kg/m³), eta_max > 0 (Pa s), grain sizes and particle compositions

Dense flowing mu(I) = mu_0 + b I, finite viscosity cap, updated compression-positive confinement, explicit zero-pressure/rate limits. Removes singular divisions and ad hoc shear-invariant factors.

Initialization rejects missing, nonfinite, nonscalar, and inadmissible parameters for these laws. beta is a plastic-potential slope, not an angle. mu in DP is the q/p slope, not tan(friction angle) or the tau/p friction coefficient used by granular flow laws. No Mohr–Coulomb fitting convention is assumed.

Bingham¶

The shear stress is s = 2 eta D', where

eta = min(mu_0, mu_s + tau_0/gamma)
gamma_c = tau_0/(mu_0-mu_s)

At zero rate, eta = mu_0. At tau_0 = 0, the law reduces to a Newtonian fluid with viscosity mu_s, including at zero rate; mu_0 >= mu_s then suffices. An optional old gamma_c input must agree with the derived transition. For simple shear the stress is continuous and becomes abs(stress_xy) = tau_0 + mu_s*abs(du/dy) above that transition. This finite-viscosity approximation permits small creep below yield; it does not represent an exactly rigid plug. The engineering shear invariant and the underlying Bingham relation are also described in the FEBio fluid material documentation.

The elastic mean stress increment is K tr(dstrain), and the instantaneous bulk viscous stress is mu_v tr(D) I. The bulk-viscous sign ensures nonnegative viscous dissipation; the old scalar implementation had the opposite sign and used a mean strain increment as though it were a volumetric one.

Drucker–Prager and its rate regularisation¶

The yield function and plastic potential are

f = q - mu*p
g = q - beta*p

For the elastic trial state, the plastic multiplier on the cone is

dlambda = max(f_trial, 0)/(3*G + K*mu*beta + eta_p/dt)
q_new = q_trial - 3*G*dlambda
p_new = p_trial + K*beta*dlambda

eta_p = 0 for dp, and eta_p = 3*G*t_star for dp_rate. Thus the rate model satisfies dlambda/dt = max(f_new, 0)/eta_p on an active surface. t_star is the shear-overstress relaxation time for zero dilation. t_star = 0 gives the rate-independent update exactly. Loading below yield and elastic unloading do not produce plastic flow. Plastic work on the cone is (q - beta*p)*dlambda >= 0 within the admitted parameter range. The use of pressure-dependent yield/flow potentials and a Perzyna flow rule follows standard viscoplasticity; see the Sandia LAMÉ theory. This implementation is the simple linear, perfectly plastic case, without that manual’s additional damage, hardening, or viscoelastic mechanisms.

The mean-tension cutoff is solved together with shear return: if the cone-only candidate has p < 0, impose p = 0 and use dlambda = q_trial/(3*G + eta_p/dt). The rate-independent case reaches the cone apex (p=q=0) without division by either invariant. The rate model can carry finite, dissipative viscous shear overstress at zero confinement; it cannot carry positive mean tension. This is a mean-stress cutoff, not a maximum-principal- stress criterion. The cone return, tension surface, and apex require separate handling, as explained in Itasca’s Drucker–Prager formulation (which uses a different shear-invariant normalisation).

Both solids use a symmetric spin split: rotate old stress by half the incremental spin, perform the constitutive update, then rotate by the other half. This is a corotational hypoelastic integration, exact for pure rigid spin with constant angular velocity. The old solver’s Lie correction is not added to this result. It is not a finite-strain hyperelastic or multiplicative plasticity model.

Linear friction¶

I = gamma * (phi @ grain_sizes) * sqrt(rho_s/p)
eta = min(eta_max, mu_0*p/gamma + b*(phi @ grain_sizes)*sqrt(rho_s*p))
s = 2 eta D'

The sum for eta is evaluated directly so p=0 and gamma=0 do not cause singular arithmetic. At p=0, stress and effective viscosity are zero and the undefined I diagnostic is recorded as zero (mu then records mu_0). At zero rate and positive confinement the effective viscosity is capped, unless mu_0=0, where the finite Newtonian limit of the second term is retained. eta and eta_limited both report the actual effective viscosity. Pressure evolves by K tr(dstrain) and is clamped to compression before computing friction. There is no arbitrary density threshold. Setting b=0 gives a capped constant-friction flowing law.

This is a dense-flow approximation. Its friction grows without bound at high I; it is not a dilute/collisional model or a claim of well-posedness over every flow regime. Local granular rheology has known continuum limitations; see Barker et al.’s stability analysis. Bingham and linear-friction fluids prescribe current stress directly, so the legacy Lie correction is not applied to their algebraic viscous stress.

Retired implementations¶

Old name

Audit finding

Replacement or decision

elastic_time

The active code uses constant initial modulus; the intended softening is commented out. An undefined phase index guards a 5% particle-mass reduction per timestep, unrelated to strain or elapsed time.

Retire. Use elastic for constant stiffness. Excavation/mass removal or modulus evolution requires a separately specified model; tunnel remains explicitly unsupported.

ken_kamrin

Unfinished duplicate local granular law: signed compressive pressure can zero its viscosity, while a gravity-based cap can make viscosity negative. Fixed grain diameter and arbitrary rate floor also bypass the intended state.

Retire this implementation; use the existing pouliquen law for the supported local friction rheology. This is not a rejection of Kamrin’s published models.

ken_simple

Uses stale shear rate and switches off stress below a hardcoded rho = 2500 kg/m³, so changing material density changes the constitutive regime arbitrarily.

Retire. linear_mu with b=0 supplies a tested constant-friction flowing alternative without that cutoff.

These names fail early with specific retirement reasons rather than silently mapping to another law. Their scalar source remains untouched in legacy/ for provenance and is excluded from the package. viscous_size has no implementation; the separate legacy P.F compressible-fluid path is also unimplemented. Neither was classified as physically invalid simply because it is missing.

Migration and checks¶

These are physical corrections and replacements, not numerical parity ports. Old coefficients may need recalibration: DP now consistently uses 3D q=sqrt(3 J2) and constant mu; dp_rate.t_star has the explicit relaxation-time meaning above. The old DP example’s unused mu(I) parameters were replaced by mu=0.5. Flowing laws use engineering shear rate, standard bulk modulus, and actual viscosity units. Their former ad hoc invariant factors are not carried across.

The DP loading examples now record growing array histories through the standard callbacks and save data/pq_history.npz plus a labelled pq_history.png. They no longer use L.S[p][i] or allocate histories from nominal timestep counts.

tests/test_constitutive.py checks analytical shear/volume responses, transition continuity, flow reversal, dissipation, hydrostatic elasticity, elastic unloading, plastic flow direction, yield consistency, cone apex, zero confinement, Perzyna relaxation and timestep convergence, tensor rotation covariance, rigid-spin integration, empty batches, parameter rejection, and output histories. Existing particle/grid/segregation regressions remain in the full suite.

The example audit now admits 33 of 37 examples for bounded smoke runs, including all seven formerly blocked Bingham/DP examples. The full dp_unit_test (50,000 steps, dt=2e-5, 1 s) and dp_rate_unit_test (5,000 steps, dt=1e-3, 5 s) also completed at their original timesteps with finite stress. The rate-independent case ended on q=0.5 p; the rate-dependent case retained the permitted positive overstress. These checks establish equation and implementation consistency; they do not replace experimental calibration, spatial convergence studies, or long runs at the old example timesteps.

The five previously supported laws retain their existing equations and stress integration. Their scalar-parity tests remain compatibility checks. In particular, legacy viscous bulk normalisation/sign and pouliquen invariant/cutoff conventions have not been brought into alignment with the newly restored laws in this audit.
